## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Cline #14195 compaction trigger using actual token count — FEATURE GAP CONFIRMED (HIGH priority, SMALL ~3-4h, carry-forward from 2026-09-17)

- **What**: Cline PR #14195 "core: trigger compaction on the provider's actual input-token count" fixed compaction trigger to use provider-reported input-token count instead of character-based estimate (~3 chars/token). Compaction's trigger compared a character-based estimate (~3 chars/token) against the model's input budget. Dense content (disassembly, image dumps, minified sources) tokenizes far denser than that, so a transcript could reach the real context ceiling while the estimate stayed under the threshold and compaction never fired. Affected runs then filled the window and had their turns squeezed down to a handful of output tokens. Fix: (1) Runtime now records the provider-reported input-token count for each request and threads it to the prepare-turn pipeline as `previousRequestInputTokens`, (2) Trigger uses `max(estimate, actual)`, so real usage crosses the threshold even when the estimate does not, (3) Estimate is kept as a floor so the very first oversized turn is still caught before any usage has been reported, (4) Compaction budget is scaled by `max(1, actual / estimate)` so retention target, message translation, and projection costs all correspond to the provider's real limit in consistent estimate units. Also raises default summarizer output budget from 4096 to 8192 (reasoning models can spend tight budget on thinking and return no summary text, skipping compaction entirely). **Verified Alexi has the bug**: `src/core/compaction.ts` line 145 `estimateMessagesTokens` uses character estimate only (chars/4 heuristic when `message.tokens.input` and `message.tokens.output` are absent), `src/core/sessionManager.ts` line 635 compaction trigger calls `shouldCompact(this.activeSession!.messages, this.maxContextTokens)` with no actual-usage parameter, `src/core/orchestrator.ts` and `src/core/streamingOrchestrator.ts` capture `usage.cache_read_input_tokens` and `usage.cache_creation_input_tokens` but NOT `usage.input_tokens` (AI SDK exposes `usage` on response, but only cache tokens are recorded). No `previousRequestInputTokens` field found on session state.
- **Why**: Dense content (disassembly, minified JS, image base64, binary dumps) tokenizes far denser than 4 chars/token. Alexi compaction uses character estimate only (`src/core/compaction.ts` line 145-169, `estimateMessagesTokens` with chars/4 fallback). Compaction never fires for dense transcripts until the provider rejects with context-window-exceeded, and affected turns get squeezed to tiny output budgets. Implementation cost ~3-4h: (1) Capture `usage.input_tokens` from provider responses in `src/core/orchestrator.ts` and `src/core/streamingOrchestrator.ts` (10 lines, AI SDK already exposes `usage.promptTokens` on response, map it to `usage.input_tokens`), (2) Store `previousRequestInputTokens` on session state (`src/core/sessionManager.ts`, 5 lines, add field to `SessionMetadata` interface), (3) Update compaction trigger in `src/core/sessionManager.ts` line 635 to use `max(estimate, actual)` (15 lines, add `previousRequestInputTokens` parameter to `shouldCompact` call, update `src/core/compaction.ts` `shouldCompact` signature to accept it), (4) Scale retention budget by `max(1, actual / estimate)` capped at `MAX_INPUT_UNDERESTIMATE_FACTOR` (20 lines, add scaling logic in `compactConversation`). Total ~50 lines, ~3-4h. This is HIGH PRIORITY — compaction failures cause user-visible quality degradation (tiny output budgets, repeated context-window errors). Carry-forward from 2026-09-17 research, now CONFIRMED with codebase verification.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14195 (Cline compaction trigger fix), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/compaction.ts (Alexi `estimateMessagesTokens` line 145-169, verified character estimate only), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/sessionManager.ts (Alexi compaction trigger line 635, verified no `previousRequestInputTokens`), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/orchestrator.ts (Alexi provider response handling, verified only cache tokens captured, not `usage.input_tokens`)
- **Category**: core (compaction, session management, context-window handling)
- **Size**: SMALL (~3-4h). HIGH PRIORITY. Capture provider-reported input-token count, thread to compaction trigger, use `max(estimate, actual)`, scale retention budget by underestimate factor. Carry-forward from 2026-09-17, CONFIRMED.

#### 2. Cline #14171 Windows CWD executable search disable — SECURITY GAP CONFIRMED (MEDIUM priority, SMALL ~2h, carry-forward from 2026-09-17)

- **What**: Cline PR #14171 "fix: stop Windows resolving bare program names through the workspace cwd" disabled Windows CWD executable search (libuv resolves a bare program name on Windows by searching the child's working directory before PATH, gated on the spawning process having `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath` defined). Cline spawns `rg`, `git`, and `powershell` with the user's workspace as cwd, so a repo shipping an `rg.exe` would get it executed at index time. Expose a one-call helper that sets Microsoft's documented opt-out (`disableCurrentDirectoryExecutableSearch()`), and call it at startup in every process that hosts Cline core: the CLI, the desktop sidecar, the VS Code extension host, and the JetBrains cline-core process. One environment variable covers every spawn site (file indexer, search, simple-git, shell executor, hooks, MCP, taskkill) and is inherited by children (cmd.exe, libuv, Bun 1.4+ honor it as well). **Verified Alexi lacks the hardening**: grep for `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath` and `disableCurrentDirectoryExecutableSearch` found zero matches in `src/`. Alexi spawns `rg` (`src/tool/tools/grep.ts`), `git` (bash commands, `src/git/autoCommit.ts` uses `simpleGit`, likely others), `powershell` (PowerShell detection in `src/core/powershell.ts`) with user workspace as cwd, so the same risk exists.
- **Why**: Security hardening. A malicious repo can ship a fake `rg.exe` or `git.exe` and get it executed by Alexi at file-search time or git operation time on Windows. Cline fixed this by setting `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath` at startup (Microsoft documented opt-out, honored by libuv, cmd.exe, Go, Bun 1.4+). Alexi spawns `rg` (grep tool), `git` (bash commands, auto-commit, apply-patch, likely others) with user workspace as cwd, so the same risk exists. Implementation cost ~2h: (1) Add `disableCurrentDirectoryExecutableSearch()` helper in `src/utils/process.ts` (~20 lines, Windows-only, sets `process.env.NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath = '1'`), (2) Call it at startup in `src/cli/program.ts` (1 line, before any tool execution, before Commander parses commands), (3) Add test planting a zero-byte `cmd.exe` in temp dir and asserting the real one still runs (~30 lines, Windows-only test with conditional skip on non-Windows). Total ~50 lines, ~2h. This is MEDIUM PRIORITY — security hardening, low likelihood (requires malicious repo + Windows + Alexi running in that repo) but high impact (arbitrary code execution). Carry-forward from 2026-09-17 research, now CONFIRMED with codebase verification.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14171 (Cline Windows CWD executable search disable), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/tool/tools/grep.ts (Alexi rg spawn, verified no `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath`), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/git/autoCommit.ts (Alexi git spawn via `simpleGit`, verified no `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath`), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/powershell.ts (Alexi PowerShell detection, verified no `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath`)
- **Category**: tools (security, Windows, spawn safety)
- **Size**: SMALL (~2h). MEDIUM PRIORITY. Add `disableCurrentDirectoryExecutableSearch()` helper, call at startup, add Windows-only test. Carry-forward from 2026-09-17, CONFIRMED.

#### 3. Cline #14225 configured subagent approvals respect delegation boundaries — NEW FEATURE GAP (MEDIUM priority, SMALL ~2-3h)

- **What**: Cline PR #14225 "fix(core): align configured subagent approvals with subagents and teammates" fixed configured subagent approvals to respect delegation boundaries (previously subagents inherited parent approvals; fix removes inherited approvals so subagents only have explicitly configured approvals passed via `task` tool `allowedTools` parameter). Commit message: "fix(core): run configured subagent tools without inherited approvals" and "test(core): verify configured delegation approval boundary". This is a permission/approval feature (subagent approval inheritance).

Cline fixed this by removing inherited approvals from subagent runtime config. Alexi likely has the same bug — needs verification in `src/tool/tools/task.ts` (task tool, subagent spawning) and `src/permission/` (approval inheritance logic). Implementation cost ~2-3h: (1) Verify Alexi subagent approval inheritance behavior in `src/tool/tools/task.ts` (10 min codebase read), (2) If bug confirmed, update subagent spawning to NOT inherit parent approvals (15 lines, remove approval inheritance in task tool, only apply `allowedTools` parameter), (3) Add test verifying subagent approval boundary (30 lines, spawn subagent with restricted approvals, assert it cannot execute unapproved tools). Total ~50 lines, ~2-3h. This is MEDIUM PRIORITY — security boundary enforcement, affects subagent isolation, but low likelihood (requires malicious subagent + inherited approvals).
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14225 (Cline configured subagent approvals fix), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/tool/tools/task.ts (Alexi task tool, needs verification), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/permission/ (Alexi approval system, needs verification)
